title: Structured intake & decision matrix for billing exceptions, commitment mapping, and marketplace offsets
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Create a repeatable, audit-friendly intake form + scored decision matrix to route customer pricing & billing requests (commitment mapping, invoice adjustments, chargebacks, marketplace offsets) to the right resolver with an SLA and required evidence. This ticket defines form fields, the scoring rubric, automated routing rules, and example outcomes so Finance, Sales-OPS, and Product can operate consistently and scale without ad-hoc emails or Slack threads.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical intake template exists in Confluence and as a reusable Typeform/Google Form with the exact fields below
Automated Linear routing rule created: submissions create PM- or FIN- prefixed issues with tags and initial assignee based on decision score
SLA definitions published and visible in the console (3 business days initial response for medium/low; 48 hours for high/urgent)
Two sample requests (commitment mapping and marketplace offset) processed end-to-end in staging and documented as runbooks
process_steps: Step 1 - Intake capture: customer-facing form collects structured evidence (customer ID, invoice number, commitment ID, requested adjustment amount, supporting docs, contract clause references)
Step 2 - Pre-validation: automated checks (verify invoice exists, commitment is active, marketplace transaction ID matches ledger) and attach result to ticket
Step 3 - Scoring: compute triage score using impact, risk, complexity, and contract terms (see triage_matrix)
Step 4 - Routing: map score to resolver pool (Billing Ops, Sales-OPS, Legal/Escalation) and set SLA and reviewers
Step 5 - Resolution: resolver documents decision with rationale, ledger adjustments, PR/GL entries, and audit log link; close with customer-facing summary template
triage_matrix: Scoring dimensions (0-3 each): Impact to customer revenue or usage (0 none - 3 severe), Financial exposure (0 - 3), Contractual clarity (0 ambiguous - 3 clear), Operational effort (0 trivial - 3 complex)
Score rules: 0-3 = Low (route to Billing Ops, SLA 10 business days), 4-7 = Medium (route to Billing Ops with Sales-OPS review, SLA 5 business days), 8-12 = High (Finance + Legal review, SLA 48 hours)
Examples: A one-off marketplace offset of $120 due to double charge -> scores: Impact 1, Exposure 1, Contract 2, Effort 1 = 5 (Medium) -> Billing Ops + Sales-OPS
Examples: Commitment mapping error affecting committed usage reconciliation for an enterprise (>$50k) -> Impact 3, Exposure 3, Contract 2, Effort 2 =10 (High) -> Finance + Legal escalation
stakeholders: Resolver pools: Billing Ops (primary), Sales-OPS (secondary), Finance (ledger adjustments), Legal (contract disputes), Customer Success (communication)
Approvals: Finance Director for adjustments > $25k, Legal for contract interpretation, VP Product for marketplace policy exceptions
notes_and_links: Existing pricing rubric references: PM-6221 and PM-12801

implementation_notes: Phase 1 (manual + automation): stand up form and webhooks, create routing rules in Linear, staffed resolve hours in Billing Ops
Phase 2 (workflow automation): Add pre-validation lambdas to verify invoice/commitment IDs and attach metadata to tickets
Phase 3 (analytics): instrument GA events for intake form fields and triage outcomes to measure triage accuracy and average resolution SLA
